title: paperclip-studios-integration-raw-notes
content:
Meeting: Kickoff — Paperclip Studios integration (11/06/2024)
Attendees: Diego (CTO), Sana (PM), Aisha (owner), Jonah, Priya

Goal (Paperclip): lightweight creative-assistant embedded in their internal dashboard for editors/QA. Requirements emphasized: low-latency preview, on-prem media indexing, strict customer data control, ability to answer questions about private assets (video transcripts + metadata).

Quick summary:
- Primary UX: editor selects a clip -> sidebar assistant returns TL;DR + scene timestamps + suggested tags + related clips. Streaming responses desired (progressive TL;DR).
- Expected peak workload: 12 concurrent editors during peak (10am-4pm), ~60 requests/minutes at peak, median request size ~300 tokens, worst-case 1200 tokens.
- Data types: transcripts (auto-generated, varying quality), video metadata (timestamps, shot labels), S3 object pointers behind VPC, thumbnails.
- Security: must run in customer's VPC or on-prem boxed deployment. No raw transcript or PHI may leave their network. Audit logs required for model calls.

Technical constraints / ask from Paperclip:
- Prefer Private deployment (VPC) with a short pilot on Dedicated if timelines demand.
- Must integrate with their internal vector DB (they currently run a self-hosted Milvus instance).
- Model behavior: want more factual/concise answers (avoid hallucinations). Ready to accept quantized open models if quality OK.
- Streaming and function/tool calling: they want assistant to call a ‘clip-fetch’ function to include exact timestamps + urls (function calling needed).

Initial thoughts / serving considerations (brainstorm):
- Deployment mode: start with Redwood Private (VPC) to satisfy data residency + logging. We can propose a short Dedicated trial if they want quicker onboarding while VPC is provisioned.
- Model selection: recommend a 7B-13B quantized candidate for interactive latency (benchmark on similar media prompts). Provide two-tier fallback policy: 1) preferred open quantized model for cost, 2) fallback to a larger low-latency hosted variant if accuracy fails.
- Batching strategy: keep per-editor requests unbatched for latency-sensitive preview flows. Use small windowed batching for background indexing/reranking tasks.
- KV cache: for repeated queries over same clip (editors often re-query current clip) — enable prefix caching to significantly reduce token cost.
- Embeddings: use 1536-d dense vectors (match Milvus schema). Provide conversion helper scripts to map our embedding outputs to their ingestion pipeline.

Gotchas / risks called out on call:
- Transcript quality variance -> will force prompt engineering with robust extraction heuristics (e.g., ignore filler tokens, collapse speaker labels). Need a small eval set.
- Timezones / playback sync: timestamps must align with editor UI expectations (ms vs sec) — confirm rounding rules.
- Milvus auth: they use token-based auth behind internal firewall; will need connector config + network egress rules.
- Cold start GPU latency for 13B models in private deployment may spike 400-800ms on first request after idle — discuss keepalive / warm pools or Dedicated reserved workers.
- Security review: their infra/security will want penetration/security checklist for Redwood Private (KMS integration, certificate rotation, data-at-rest encryption) — compile a short doc for review.

Concrete acceptance criteria (what success looks like for pilot):
- End-to-end assistant in staging: clip selected -> streaming TL;DR within 600ms p50, 1.2s p95 for 300-token requests.
- Accurate timestamped suggestions: +/- 500ms alignment with editor UI for top-3 suggestions.
- Embedding recall: vector search returns relevant clips in top-5 for 80% of sample queries (we'll define eval set).
- No raw transcripts leave VPC. Audit logs available for 30 days in their SIEM.

Action items / next steps (owner / due):
- Aisha: draft short technical checklist for Paperclip security team (KMS, TLS, audit hooks, IP allowlist). Due: 11/08/2024.
- Jonah: perf-estimates + initial model candidates (quantized 7B/13B) with local latency numbers (run on equivalent A100 / 80GB profile). Due: 11/13/2024.
- Priya: prepare small eval prompt set (25 transcripts of varying noise/length) and baseline metrics (hallucination rate, timestamp alignment). Due: 11/12/2024.
- Diego/Sana: share Milvus connection details + sample transcript bundle (anonymized) and list of columns/metadata. Due: 11/09/2024.
- Set up follow-up deep-dive: API/infra + security working session (in-person optional). Proposed: 11/14/2024 09:00 PT.

Open questions to clarify on next call:
- Can Paperclip accept model logs (prompt/response hashes) for debugging, or must we restrict to local-only logs? (Sanitization required).
- Any regulatory constraints re: PII in transcripts beyond internal policy? Need a short written policy.
- Are editors using offline mode? If yes, how will caching work across disconnected clients?

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider building a small local ‘prompt sanitizer’ microservice that strips PII before embedding/serving and runs inside their VPC. Good sales-ops artifact.
- Potential upsell: Redwood Optimize suggestions after pilot (quantization profile + batching tuning) to shave costs 20–40%.

Meeting end: overall good fit; Paperclip motivated by privacy + low-latency UX. Pilot looks scoped enough for 4–6 week technical sprint if Milvus + sample data arrive quickly.

Raw prompt examples captured on call (for eval set):
1) "Summarize this clip in three bullets. Include scene timestamps for the part where the speaker says 'we'll ship tomorrow'."
2) "Suggest three short tags and list related clips with similar dialogue (max 5)."
3) "Given this transcript, what are the top 2 action items mentioned and their timestamps?"

End notes: save eval set in GH under repo 'paperclip-integration/evals', coordinate with security checklist.

----
Personal scratch bits:
- Keep the initial model small and conservative (penalize hallucination with temperature=0.0-ish + system prompt instructing abstain).
- Check their editor UI framerate — streaming chunk cadence matters, aim for <150ms per chunk to feel responsive.
- Reminder: include a short pricing estimate for pilot (1 month Dedicated burst + VPC infra sampling) to avoid procurement delays.
summary: Kickoff notes for Paperclip Studios integration pilot: private/VPC deployment, streaming assistant for video editors, Milvus integration, evaluative prompts, action items assigned, security checklist requested.
